senses.gloss: स्यन्दन- + आरोह स्यन्दन- + आरोह, m. a warrior who fights in a car.
श्याल- + नामन् श्याल- + नामन्, adj. called after the name of his brother-in-law, ib.
श्यान श्यान, see श्वि.

श्याम श्याम (probably from श्वि, cf. श्येत),
 I. adj., f. मा.
 1. Green.
 2. Dark-blue, Vikr. d. 26.
 3. Black, Bhartṛ. 2, 14; 36 (dry ?); shady, Utt. Rāmac. 42, 8.
 4. Brown, Hiḍ. 2, 25; Nal. 12, 50; 18, 11.
 II. m.
 1. Green, black (the colour).
 2. A cloud.
 3. The कोकिल or Indian cuckoo.
 4. A sacred fig-tree at प्रयाग, Utt. Rāmac. 15, 11; cf. Wilson, Hind. Theat. 2. ed. i. 302, n. †.
 5. Thorn-apple.
 III. m., and f. मा, A sort of grain, Panicum frumentaceum.
 IV. f. मा.
 1. Night.
 2. Shade, shadow.
 3. The female of the Indian cuckoo, Pañc. 157, 4.
 4. A cow.
 5. Durgā.
 6. A married woman before she has borne children.
 7. A plant, commonly Priyaṅgn, Megh. 102; and name of several others.
 V. n.
 1. Pepper.
 2. Sea salt.
 --Cf. κύανος.

श्यामल श्याम + ल,
 I. adj., f. ला, Of a dark-blue or black colour, Daśak. in Chr. 190, 13; blackish, Mālat. 145, 10.
 II. m.
 1. Black (the colour).
 2. Pepper.
 3. The religious fig-tree.
 4. A large bee.
 III. f. ला, Pārvatī.
श्यामाक श्यामाक (cf. श्याम), m. A sort of grain, Panicum frumentaceum, Śāk. d. 89.
श्यामाय श्यामाय, a denomin. derived from श्याम with य, Ātm. To become black, to prove impure (as gold, cf. the next), Mālav. d. 30.
श्यामिका श्यामिका, i. e. श्याम + क, f. Impurity (of gold), Ragh. 1, 10.

स्यमीक स्यमीक,
 I. m.
 1. An anthill.
 2. A particular tree.
 3. Time.
 4. Cloud.
 II. f. का, Indigo.
श्यामित श्यामित, i. e. श्याम + इत, adj. Blackened, discoloured, Kir. 16, 2.
श्याल श्याल, see स्याल.

स्याल स्याल, and श्याल श्याल,
 I. m.
 1. A wife's brother, Bhag. 1, 34 (श्).
 2. The favourite of a king, Rājat. 5, 451 (? श्).
 II. f. ली, A wife's sister.
 --Cf. ἀέλιοι.
श्यालक श्याल + क, m. A miserable brother-in-law, Cāṇ. 80 in Berl. Monatsb. 1864, 412.
श्याव श्याव (akin to श्याम), adj. Of a brown colour, livid, Daśak. in Chr. 187, 13.
स्यद स्यद, i. e. स्यन्द् + अ, m. Speed, Nalod. 4, 6.

स्यन्द् स्यन्द्, i. 1, Ātm., and in the aor., fut., and condit., Par.
 1. To drop, to distill, Lass. 59, 5.
 2. To flow, MBh. 1, 3990.
 3. To run, Nal. 13, 10.
 --With the prep. अभि अभि (ष्यन्द् and स्यन्द्), To rain on, Utt. Rāmac. 16, 10; 133, 9 (हृदयं स्नेहेन, To flow, to melt with love).
 --With नि नि (ष्यन्द् and स्यन्द्), To flow, Bhāg. P. 6, 9, 38.

स्यन्दन स्यन्द् + अन,
 I. adj. Quick, Kir. 15, 16.
 II. m.
 1. A war chariot, Hit. iii. d. 81.
 2. Air.
 3. A tree, [] Dalbergia ougeinensis, Nal. 12, 3.
 II. f. नी, Saliva.
 IV. n.
 1. Oozing, Bhāṣāp. 6; 155.
 2. Water.
 3. Going swiftly.
स्यन्दनिका स्यन्दनिका, i. e. स्यन्दनी + क, f. A drop of saliva, Rām. 3, 53, 56.

स्यन्दिन् स्यन्द् + इन्,
 I. adj., f. नी.
 1. Oozing, trickling, Utt. Rāmac. 23, 3.
 2. Going.
 II. f. नी.
 1. Saliva.
 2. A cow bearing twins.
 --Comp.

† स्यम् स्यम्, i. 1, Par.
 1. To sound.
 2. To go.
 --i. 10, Ātm. To consider, to think.
स्यमन्तक स्यमन्तक, m. The gem worn by Kṛṣṇa.
